version.changelog:
openai-ads v1.1.2

- Updated the logo graphic (assets/logo.svg) for improved branding or visual clarity.
- No functional or documentation changes.

llm.summary: This skill is an ads-management integration with real credential and spending authority, but its onboarding and API client create avoidable credential-exposure risks.

dimensions.detail: Network access to an ads API is purpose-aligned, but scripts/openai_ads_client.py allows OPENAI_ADS_BASE_URL to redirect authenticated requests while still attaching the bearer API key.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package appears to install as a normal OpenClaw/Hermes skill with no post-install hook or bundled dependency installer observed, but the docs ask users to configure a Habilis MCP server and bearer token.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the assistant to ask for API credentials through chat, says it can save and test them, and triggers an automatic health check after receiving them; that is under-scoped for privileged ad-account credentials.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No cron, startup hook, or local backdoor persistence was observed, but the skill requests privileged API credentials and can mutate remote advertising state without confirmation, dry-run, or spending guardrails.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Managing campaigns, ads, insights, audiences, feeds, and conversion tracking is coherent with the stated ads-manager purpose, but the artifacts describe high-impact live advertising operations and some capabilities more broadly than the bundled scripts implement.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Do not paste API keys into chat; configure them only through a secure environment or secret manager. Use narrowly scoped ads credentials, spending limits, and key rotation. Treat create, pause, archive, feed, audience, and conversion actions as live account mutations, and avoid using the configurable OPENAI_ADS_BASE_URL path unless it is pinned to a trusted HTTPS origin.
llm.findings:
[SSD-3] unexpected: Accepted: the required first-run workflow and sample message explicitly allow pasting an OpenAI Ads API key into chat and imply saving/testing it, which is not appropriate secret handling.
[TT3] unexpected: Accepted: scripts/openai_ads_client.py builds the request origin from OPENAI_ADS_BASE_URL and sends Authorization to it, so an environment override can forward the bearer credential to an unintended host.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted in substance: the static scan's two material points are supported by the artifacts, namely chat-based credential collection and the configurable authenticated API origin.
[SQP-2] unexpected: Partially accepted: external ad, audience, lead, catalog, and conversion data flows are expected for this purpose, but the artifacts lack adequate privacy, consent, and confirmation warnings for those flows and live mutations.
[E1] expected: Downgraded as a standalone issue: sending campaign and ad data to an external ads API is core functionality, not exfiltration by itself.
[TP4] unexpected: Accepted as a disclosure concern: the description promises autonomous end-to-end management including CAPI, audiences, and feeds, while the bundled CLI mainly implements account, campaign, ad group, ad, preview, and insights operations.
[PE3] expected: Downgraded: references to access tokens and API keys are expected for an authenticated ads integration and do not show credential-file theft.
[RA2] unexpected: Not accepted: inspected artifacts did not show cron jobs, startup scripts, background workers, or local state persistence mechanisms.
